one_liner: A Bengaluru-based app that automatically rounds up UPI payments and invests the spare change into 24k digital gold.
recommendation_rationale: Jar has real scale and reached profitability in its last two reported quarters, but its core product is currently the subject of an active criminal FIR under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, an RBI market-surveillance alert, and a public SEBI warning that digital/e-gold trading is unregulated. That combination is a legal and regulatory risk large enough to pass on until the investigation is resolved, regardless of the financial metrics.

snapshot.founded: 2021 (exact month reported inconsistently across sources; approximated as mid-2021 for the years-since-founding calculation below)
snapshot.stage: Post-Series B; a larger round was reported in advanced talks in December 2025 but was not confirmed closed as of this research
snapshot.total_funding_display: USD 59.1 M disclosed across seed + Series A + Series B (per press reports; no single primary source gives a cumulative total directly -- see unresolved gaps). A further USD 100M+ round at a reported USD 500-550M term-sheet valuation was in talks as of December 2025, not confirmed closed.
snapshot.last_round: Series B: USD 22.6 M led by Tiger Global at over USD 300 M valuation (August 2022, per Entrackr's restatement of the round)

business_model: Jar links to a user's UPI payment history and automatically invests small round-up amounts, starting from INR 10, into 24k digital gold, aiming to build a low-friction savings habit for first-time investors.[^3][^5] Gold bought through the app is held via a vaulting partner (BRINKS, per the company's own site) and insured through ICICI Lombard.[^5] In FY25 the company reported it had vertically integrated its gold stack: rather than only routing user savings through external gold partners, Jar became a principal seller that owns and manages more of the gold value chain itself, which is also why its gross revenue figure jumped sharply that year (see traction section).[^1]
why_now: Jar reported reaching profitability in its last two consecutive quarters (January-March 2025 and April-June 2025) after years of scaling losses, and was reportedly in advanced talks as of December 2025 to raise over USD 100 million led by Westbridge at a term-sheet valuation of USD 500-550 million, roughly 1.7-1.8x its 2022 Series B valuation.[^1][^2] Set against that is a live regulatory overhang: an FIR filed in January under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, an RBI market-surveillance alert in July 2025, and a SEBI public warning in November 2025 that digital/e-gold trading is currently unregulated.[^4] Whether the pending round closes, and on what terms, may depend on how that investigation resolves.
market_and_competition: Jar competes in India's digital-gold savings space alongside providers such as SafeGold, MMTC-PAMP and Augmont, with gold-buying features also embedded in larger platforms like PhonePe and Groww.[^6] This competitor picture was retrieved via a search-engine summary of generic comparison-blog content rather than a dedicated competitive analysis, and should be treated as low-confidence market colour rather than a verified competitive assessment.
traction_and_team: Jar reported FY25 (year ended March 2025) operating revenue of INR 208 crore.[^1] Following the vertical integration of its gold stack, the company also reported a much larger gross revenue figure of INR 2,450 crore for the same year, which reflects booking the full value of gold transactions now that Jar acts as principal rather than intermediary -- this is a change in what is being measured, not a like-for-like continuation of the INR 208 crore operating-revenue trend, and the two figures should not be added or averaged.[^1] Net losses (excluding ESOP costs) were INR 35.23 crore in FY25, and the company says it was profitable in its last two reported quarters.[^1] No FY24 comparison figure was found in the sources retrieved for this run, so FY25's reported growth could not be independently checked against a prior-year base. The company reports over 35 million registered users across 12,000 pin codes (its own site claims 4+ crore, i.e. 40 million+, which is higher than the press-reported figure and not reconciled here).[^1][^5] Founders Nishchay Ag (CEO) and Misbah Ashraf (Chief Product Officer) started the company in 2021 with a USD 4.5 million seed round, reaching a USD 32 million Series A within about seven months at a valuation of over USD 200 million.[^3]

valuation.label: valuation
valuation.definition: Series B post-money valuation floor ('over USD 300 million'), August 2022, per Entrackr's restatement of the round. This is the last CONFIRMED, closed-round valuation; the USD 500-550M figure from the December 2025 term sheet is excluded here because that round was not confirmed closed.

total_capital_raised.label: total_capital_raised
total_capital_raised.definition: Sum of press-reported round sizes: USD 4.5M seed + USD 32M Series A + USD 22.6M Series B. No single primary source discloses this cumulative figure directly; treat as an approximation.

years_since_founding.label: years_since_founding
years_since_founding.definition: Years from Jar's approximate founding (mid-2021, exact month inconsistently reported) to 2022-08-18, the same date the total_capital_raised figure is measured as of (the Series B close). This is the correct pairing for capital_raised_per_year: measuring 'years since founding' to today (over 5 years later, with no further confirmed raises in this figure) would understate the true early fundraising pace by roughly 4.6x.
years_since_founding.notes: Founding month approximated as 2021-07-01 based on the Series A article's 'seven months old' reference at its February 2022 announcement; precise to roughly +/- 2-3 months. Corrected 2026-09-18: an earlier version of this run measured years to the report-generation date instead of to the capital-raised date, which understated capital_raised_per_year (showed ~USD 11.3M/year instead of the correct ~USD 52.3M/year).

annual_revenue.label: annual_revenue
annual_revenue.definition: FY25 (year ended March 2025) operating revenue, i.e. net of the gold pass-through booked after vertical integration -- the more comparable of the two FY25 figures Jar reported.

gross_revenue_fy25_post_vertical_integra.label: gross_revenue_fy25_post_vertical_integration
gross_revenue_fy25_post_vertical_integra.definition: FY25 'gross/total revenue' after Jar became principal seller of gold (owns and manages the gold value chain, books full transaction value). Deliberately tagged as GMV-like rather than 'revenue' in this schema so it is never mixed into the standard revenue-based checks alongside the INR 208 Cr operating-revenue figure -- the brief this project follows specifically warns against mixing GMV and revenue, and this is a real example of exactly that risk.

net_loss_fy25.label: net_loss_fy25
net_loss_fy25.definition: FY25 net loss excluding ESOP costs.

pending_round_valuation_unconfirmed.label: pending_round_valuation_unconfirmed
pending_round_valuation_unconfirmed.definition: Midpoint of the reported USD 500-550 million term-sheet valuation for the Westbridge-led round. NOT used in valuation_multiple because the round was not confirmed closed as of the source's December 2025 report date.
pending_round_valuation_unconfirmed.notes: Deliberately excluded from the standard valuation Fact above; keep it out of any claim check unless the round is confirmed closed in a later run.

claims.text: Jar reported FY25 operating revenue of INR 208 crore.
Jar reported FY25 gross revenue of INR 2,450 crore following vertical integration of its gold stack.
Jar's FY25 net loss, excluding ESOP costs, was INR 35.23 crore, and the company was profitable in its last two reported quarters.
Jar was in advanced talks as of December 2025 to raise over USD 100 million led by Westbridge at a USD 500-550 million term-sheet valuation, not yet confirmed closed.
Jar's Series B (August 2022) raised USD 22.6 million led by Tiger Global at over USD 300 million valuation.
Jar's Series A (February 2022) raised USD 32 million at over USD 200 million valuation, following a USD 4.5 million seed round.
An FIR was filed against Jar under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, and RBI and SEBI separately raised concerns about the legality/regulatory status of digital gold trading.
Jar's directors obtained anticipatory bail and the CID investigation is ongoing.
Jar reports over 35 million registered users across 12,000 pin codes.
Jar's own website claims it is trusted by 4+ crore (40 million+) Indians.
Jar's competitors include SafeGold, MMTC-PAMP and Augmont, with digital gold features also offered by PhonePe and Groww.

risks.risk: Jar's core product is under active legal and regulatory scrutiny: a criminal FIR under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, an RBI market-surveillance alert, and a SEBI public warning that digital/e-gold trading is unregulated.
risks.mitigant: Ask for the current legal status of the CID investigation, any formal regulator correspondence, and outside counsel's written assessment of business-model risk under the BUDS Act and possible future SEBI/RBI regulation.

risks.risk: FY25's headline revenue figures mix a comparable operating-revenue base (INR 208 Cr) with a much larger gross figure (INR 2,450 Cr) that reflects an accounting/business-model change (becoming principal seller), not organic growth, and no FY24 baseline was found to check the growth claims independently.
risks.mitigant: Request FY24 audited operating revenue on the same basis as FY25, plus a plain walkthrough (with cost of goods sold) of how the INR 2,450 Cr gross figure is constructed.

risks.risk: The reported USD 100M+ Westbridge-led round at a USD 500-550M valuation was described as 'in talks' with a term sheet, not closed, as of the December 2025 report; relying on that valuation before it closes could be premature.
risks.mitigant: Confirm deal status, final terms and closing date directly with the company before using any valuation above the confirmed August 2022 Series B figure.

risks.risk: Public reporting mixes currencies (INR for revenue, USD for valuation and funding) and gives inconsistent user-count figures (35M per press vs 40M+ per the company's own site), which blocks computing a like-for-like valuation multiple from public sources alone.
risks.mitigant: Request a single-currency data room (cap table, P&L, and a defined user/customer metric) directly from the company rather than relying on press aggregation.

what_would_change_recommendation: A move away from Pass would need the regulatory investigation to be resolved or clearly narrowed (charges dropped, or Jar demonstrating registration/compliance that satisfies RBI and SEBI's stated concerns), plus a like-for-like FY24-to-FY25 operating revenue comparison from the company directly. Further regulatory escalation, or the reported financing round falling through because of the investigation, would confirm the Pass.
founder_questions: What is the current status of the Koramangala CID investigation and the BUDS Act FIR, and what specific steps has Jar taken in response to the RBI's July 2025 surveillance alert and SEBI's November 2025 public warning?
Can you share FY24 audited operating revenue on the same basis as the FY25 INR 208 crore figure, so growth can be assessed like-for-like?
Walk us through exactly how the FY25 INR 2,450 crore gross revenue figure is constructed under the new vertically-integrated model, including the associated cost of gold procured.
What is the actual current status of the reported Westbridge-led round -- is it closed, and if so at what valuation and on what terms?
If digital or e-gold trading is formally classified as a regulated activity, what licence(s) would Jar need, from which regulator, and what is the plan and timeline to obtain them?
unresolved_gaps: Valuation (USD) and operating revenue (INR) are reported in different currencies by the sources found in this research pass; a valuation multiple was not computed because doing so would require an unsourced FX-rate and timing assumption. This is a live example of the currency-mismatch guardrail this project's claim checks are built to enforce, not a gap that should be closed by guessing an exchange rate.

No FY24 (or earlier) operating revenue figure was found, so the multiple press reports of a 'ninefold' FY25 revenue rise could not be independently corroborated from a directly-fetched source and were deliberately left out of the memo's prose rather than repeated as fact.
The reported USD 100M+ Westbridge-led round (December 2025, term sheet at a USD 500-550M valuation) was not confirmed closed as of this research date.
Total capital raised (~USD 59.1M) is a sum of individually press-reported round sizes, not a figure disclosed directly by any single source; treat it as an approximation.
User-count figures differ across sources (35 million per Entrackr/press vs 4+ crore / 40 million+ per Jar's own website) and were not reconciled.
Exact founding month is inconsistently reported across sources; 2021-07-01 was used as an approximation for the years-since-founding calculation.

ARPU (monthly revenue per paying customer) is not computed for Jar: no source discloses a 'paying customer' count in the subscription/seat sense, and Jar's revenue comes from per-transaction gold purchases rather than a subscription. Even if a customer count were found, ARPU may not be a economically meaningful metric for this business model -- this is a not-applicable case, not just a missing-data one.
